summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of Fixed Deposit taxation in India, but some key figures regarding TDS thresholds and Form 15G/15H eligibility are outdated for the current financial year (FY 2025-26 onwards).

claims.claim: Interest earned on a Fixed Deposit is classified under the head 'Income from Other Sources' as per the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that FD interest is taxed under 'Income from Other Sources' as per the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: Banks deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) if your FD interest exceeds ₹40,000 (₹50,000 for senior citizens) in a financial year.
claims.note: For FY 2025-26 onwards, the TDS threshold for individuals below 60 years is ₹50,000, and for senior citizens, it is ₹1,00,000. The article's figures are for FY 2024-25.

claims.claim: If you have not provided your PAN, the TDS rate jumps to 20%.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that if PAN is not provided, the TDS rate on FD interest is 20%.

claims.claim: If your total income for the financial year is below the basic exemption limit (e.g., ₹2.5 lakhs for individuals below 60, ₹3 lakhs for senior citizens), you can submit Form 15G (for non-senior citizens) or Form 15H (for senior citizens) to your bank.
claims.note: Forms 15G and 15H can be submitted to avoid TDS if total income is below the basic exemption limit. The basic exemption limits mentioned (₹2.5 lakhs for individuals below 60, ₹3 lakhs for senior citizens) are consistent with the old tax regime.

claims.claim: Tax-Saving FDs come with a mandatory lock-in period of 5 years.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that Tax-Saving FDs have a mandatory lock-in period of 5 years.

claims.claim: The principal amount invested in these FDs, up to a maximum of ₹1.5 lakhs in a financial year, is eligible for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that the maximum deduction under Section 80C for investments, including tax-saving FDs, is ₹1.5 lakhs per financial year.

claims.claim: For cumulative FDs, the interest is taxable on an accrual basis each financial year, even if you don't physically receive it until maturity.
claims.note: Sources confirm that interest on cumulative FDs is taxable on an accrual basis annually, even if received at maturity.

article_title: Fixed Deposits: Tax on FD Interest & Key Rules for Depositors
